name: Quorum
description: A single-file H5 ranked-ballot app drawn as a polling-station paper. Twenty ballots are already in, grouped into six blocs, and the app runs an instant runoff over them — count first preferences, eliminate the lowest, move those papers to their next surviving choice, repeat — re-running the entire count on every action. Yours is the twenty-first paper and it is drawn up by ranking rather than picking, which makes the whole thing a fixed point rather than a lookup. On the twenty seeded papers the last round is a dead heat, so one ballot decides it, but not in the obvious way: who you put first is often irrelevant because your paper ends up wherever your later preferences send it. 5 screens, 5 candidates, a round-by-round table, exhausting ballots, and a deterministic tie-break.

finish.answer: final answer for question tasks; optional for action tasks

observation.text: engine.a11y(state) — the ballot paper, every round's counts, the majority needed, exhausted papers and where each eliminated candidate's votes went all serialise, so the count is fully checkable without pixels.
observation.pixels: 390x844 screenshot (browser backend); __ENV__.bounds() maps every test-id to a pixel box
observation.state: engine.snapshot(state) — canonical state plus a derived view holding both the live preview result and the official one. For the verifier only.

world.method: instant runoff: lowest count eliminated each round, papers move to their next surviving preference, a majority of the live (non-exhausted) papers wins
world.ties: elimination ties break on round-one first preferences, then on the earlier name; the same rule settles a two-way dead heat at the end
world.seeded: 20 papers in six blocs; first preferences Morag 6, Esi 5, Tan 4, Priya 3, Jude 2; eliminated in the order Jude, Priya, Esi; the last round is 10–10
world.quorum: 21 papers, so without yours the poll does not stand
world.pivot: Morag first elects Morag and Tan first elects Tan, but Esi, Priya or Jude first elects whichever of Morag and Tan you put next — and no paper without Tan on it anywhere can elect Tan
